# TokenShade

> Stop the burn on your plan.

TokenShade is an independent, open-source orchestration policy for coding
agents. It groups independent, already-known tool calls, preserves sequential
work when order matters, and discourages repetitive polling. It is Codex-first
with a one-session prompt for ChatGPT Work, a Claude Code adapter, a Kimi Code
CLI adapter, and agent-neutral instruction files. Ordinary ChatGPT chats
without agent tools have nothing to batch; the benchmark claim is Codex-only.

## One-tweet prompt

Build me a skill based on TokenShade (https://tokenshade.vercel.app). Layer batching and polling rules over my setup; preserve instructions. Keep dependencies, exploration, approvals, conflicting writes, waits, and resumes sequential. Show dry-run and diff first.

## Public benchmark

Across five matched Sol/XHigh serial-control/TokenShade pairs, observed median
model cycles fell from 8 to 1 (87.5% fewer) and median total tokens fell from
243,314 to 70,085 (71.2% fewer), with the same eight-file coverage and
conclusions. This is a bounded mechanism benchmark, not a universal savings
promise or a comparison against default Sol.

## Canonical resources

- Website: https://tokenshade.vercel.app
- Repository: https://github.com/frizas/tokenshade
- Installation: https://tokenshade.vercel.app/#install
- Full prompt pack: https://github.com/frizas/tokenshade/blob/main/PROMPTS.md
- Honest numbers: https://github.com/frizas/tokenshade/blob/main/docs/HONEST-NUMBERS.md
- Privacy: https://github.com/frizas/tokenshade/blob/main/PRIVACY.md
- Security: https://github.com/frizas/tokenshade/blob/main/SECURITY.md

The TokenShade software has no telemetry or backend. The public website uses
consent-based aggregate analytics. TokenShade is not affiliated with OpenAI.
Benchmark claims are workload-specific.
